preamble: Velar fronting, the replacement of velar stops by alveolars (/ɡ/ > [d], /k/ > [t]), is one of the most frequent phonological processes in children acquiring English, usually gone by about age 4. In some children it is positional, affecting only word-initial or stressed-syllable onsets. No regular diachronic sound change of plain [ɡ] to [d] is known; historical velar-to-coronal shifts go through palatalization and end in affricates or sibilants (ɡ > dʒ, dz, z), and Greek δ from *gʷ involves a labiovelar.
